papers.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) face significant scalability challenges in long-video understanding due to quadratic attention complexity and context window constraints. Existing retrieval-based approaches typically rely on supervised learning from static keyframe annotations. However, these label priors often fail to align with the actual information required by downstream MLLMs for complex reasoning, creating a misalignment between the training target and inference needs. To bridge this gap, we propose a probabilistic framework that reformulates frame selection as latent-variable inference. We first initialize a lightweight policy using supervised learning to capture general visual saliency. Then, we treat a frozen MLLM as a task environment and use its answer likelihood as dense task evidence to refine the policy via Bayesian Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). Within this formulation, the negative log-likelihood (NLL) over ground-truth answer tokens provides a principled dense reward, while a prior-matching KL term preserves semantic consistency with the elicited label prior. This process transitions the selection principle from static label priors to task evidence. Extensive experiments on Video-MME, MLVU, and LongVideoBench demonstrate that our selector achieves competitive accuracy with MLLM-based scorers while retaining the inference efficiency of lightweight methods. The selector is trained once with a frozen MLLM environment and transfers directly to multiple downstream MLLMs without retraining. Code is available at \url{github.com/Miraclecsc/Frame_Selection_GRPO}.

analysis.key_results: 在Video-MME、MLVU和LongVideoBench数据集上，所提选择器达到与基于MLLM的评分器相当的精度，同时保留轻量方法的推理效率；训练一次后可直接迁移到多个下游MLLM而无需重新训练。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出一种概率框架，将帧选择重新定义为潜变量推断，通过贝叶斯GRPO使用冻结MLLM的任务证据（答案似然）优化轻量策略，弥合训练目标与推理需求之间的不一致。
analysis.method: 先用监督学习初始化轻量策略捕捉视觉显著性；再将冻结MLLM视为任务环境，利用其答案似然作为稠密证据，通过贝叶斯组相对策略优化（GRPO）细化策略；其中负对数似然提供稠密奖励，先验匹配KL项保持语义一致性。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 本文提出一种基于贝叶斯GRPO的概率框架，将长视频理解的帧选择从静态标签先验转向任务证据，在保持轻量级效率的同时达到与MLLM评分器相当的精度。

papers.abstract: World models offer increasingly rich environments for exploration, yet intervening in a world while observing the consequences from freely chosen viewpoints remains challenging. We tackle these challenges by introducing UniState, a framework for controllable world simulation built on a unified world-state representation. This representation unifies spatial memory and user interventions. Users specify object motion directly within spatial memory, while independently choosing the camera trajectory from which the resulting world state is observed. This unification makes the relationship between the scene and the requested changes explicit, removing ambiguity between object motion and viewpoint change from the control specification. Crucially, specifying an intervention does not require prescribing every resulting movement: the video model can synthesize additional motion within controlled objects and plausible interactions with their surroundings. We develop training and sampling strategies that help generated videos follow the specified object motion and camera trajectory while preserving this capacity to generate responses beyond the prescribed transformations. Experiments demonstrate more accurate joint object and camera control than the existing methods, alongside qualitative evidence that intervention-induced scene changes persist across rollouts.

papers.abstract: Onboard inference latency creates a mismatch between the trajectories predicted by vision-language-action (VLA) policies and the ongoing motion of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). We present AeroDASH, an asynchronous VLA framework for continuous language-conditioned flight. A B-spline policy is initialized through supervised fine-tuning on expert demonstrations, providing continuous trajectory references in position and yaw. During execution, trajectory fusion removes the expired prediction prefix and connects the remaining segment to the active reference with derivative continuity while limiting trajectory deformation. To account for deviations induced by asynchronous execution, execution-aware group relative policy optimization (GRPO) further adapts the policy using trajectory-level rewards. On the UAV-Flow test set, AeroDASH achieves a success rate of 76.56%, exceeding OpenVLA-UAV and AeroDASH w/o GRPO by 38.1 and 20.1 percentage points, respectively. Execution experiments show that AeroDASH sustains motion during inference and reduces acceleration, jerk, and speed fluctuations relative to asynchronous tracking of waypoint sequences. We further demonstrate language-conditioned flight with onboard inference and asynchronous trajectory execution. The code will be released upon acceptance.

papers.abstract: For practical motion generation, it is essential to handle multimodality (multiple actions can be correct for the same observation) while maintaining low inference cost and strong generalization from limited demonstrations. We introduce an attentive mixture-density policy trained with the Energy Score that represents future visuomotor trajectories as explicit probability distributions with a single forward pass. Concretely, we output Gaussian mixture parameters for joint commands (and optionally attention points) and optimize them with the Energy Score (computed as a sum of 1D CRPS under a diagonal covariance assumption) instead of the negative log-likelihood (NLL) to avoid MDN singularities and gradient-scale instabilities. Our architecture couples explicit spatial attention with mixture-density outputs, enabling robust multimodal behavior selection under visual noise and small-data regimes. On an 8-DOF manipulator, the method generates distinct avoidance trajectories and stabilizes learning in obstacle avoidance. Moreover, in a randomized moving-object grasping task, where spatiotemporal multimodality and fast timing decisions are required, the proposed model outperforms Diffusion Policy by 15-25% under several unseen conditions, demonstrating superior generalization and real-time feasibility.

papers.abstract: World models are increasingly judged by how well they rank plausible futures, yet plausibility alone is the wrong target. The same scene can evolve under many latent rules, and a future that is smooth and physically valid under one rule can be incoherent under the rule actually in force. We formalize the resulting failure, operator-blindness, and show that it is systematically hidden by standard evaluation: a scorer can attain near-perfect generic ranking while separating current-world from other-world futures no better than chance. We introduce Operator-Mismatch Contrastive (OMC) learning, whose semantic hard negatives are valid-but-wrong-operator trajectories, and a matching protocol that measures world-relative coherence directly. On a controlled synthetic benchmark with in- and out-of-distribution operator parameters, across two trajectory-scoring backbones, and on feature-level external validation with CoPhy ballsCF, OMC raises operator-sensitive scoring far above a chance baseline that nonetheless achieves 0.99 generic top-1. We prove that the wrong-operator negative is necessary both for the protocol to detect the failure and for the objective to fix it, and position OMC as an auxiliary coherence signal (a trajectory-coherence scorer, not a generative model, planner, or control agent) that can be attached to existing world-model representations.

analysis.key_results: 在受控合成基准（分布内和分布外算子参数）和CoPhy ballsCF特征级外部验证中，OMC大幅提升算子敏感评分，远超仍能达到0.99通用Top-1的随机基线。

papers.abstract: Emerging Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) are moving beyond representation learning towards latent world models that support prediction, planning, and control. Yet their latent worlds naturally lack a human-interpretable interface. In this Perspective, we argue that as JEPA latents become internal states for prediction and action, interpretability must move beyond what they encode to how latent variables interact, evolve, and causally drive prediction. To this end, we envision a four-stage research agenda, involving Ground, Structure, Verify, and Act, to guide this shift toward actionable latent-world understanding. Within our framework, existing JEPA interpretability efforts provide early evidence for Ground, while systematic analysis of latent structure, causal verification, and intervention remains largely unexplored. Overall, this Perspective aims to call for a broader latent-world interpretability agenda that shifts attention from decoding representations toward understanding, validating, and acting on latent worlds.

papers.abstract: General purpose multimodal language models (LMs) are increasingly capable of directly controlling robotic arms (e.g., by commanding end effector poses) to manipulate their environment. Tracking the development of these capabilities is important for understanding their potential benefits, such as improving industrial automation, and risks, such as enabling malicious users to produce dangerous chemical or biological agents. To this end, we investigate the ability of frontier multimodal LMs to directly control physical robotic arms. We evaluate seven models at multiple reasoning-effort settings on six manipulation tasks taken from the RoboDojo benchmark. To our knowledge, this is the first systematic comparison of a broad range of frontier LMs across a common suite of manipulation tasks on physical hardware. We find that current frontier models can directly control real robotic arms to perform a variety of manipulation tasks but are not yet precise or efficient enough to complete them within a practical action budget. However, these capabilities are improving rapidly: performance increases on our benchmark between July and September 2026 (inclusive) correspond to a performance doubling time of 44.5 days, while the best recorded execution rate increased by a factor of 4.4 and the lowest recorded execution cost fell by a factor of 6.2. These trends raise the possibility that the Bitter Lesson is coming to robotics; the capabilities of embodied general purpose LMs may one day be comparable to those of more specialized models.

papers.abstract: The success of chain-of-thought (CoT) in complex reasoning can be attributed to a textual scaffolding effect: explicit intermediate results can be examined, reused, and composed to support subsequent reasoning, much as scaffolding supports a building under construction. However, mainstream multimodal LLMs lack an equivalent scaffold for visual distinctions that are difficult to express in concise verbal descriptions. We therefore ask: Can native visual representations become first-class citizens alongside language, providing a visual scaffold for reasoning? We define native multimodal reasoning as reasoning in which native visual representations and language jointly carry reusable intermediate states. As a concrete implementation, the visual scaffolding mechanism we proposed lets the MLLM autonomously initiate a retrieval action at any reasoning step. A lightweight retriever selects native visual features, which are then incorporated directly into the evolving CoT and remain available to subsequent steps. To evaluate this mechanism under controlled visual demands, we introduce NMR-Bench, comprising Burden Counting and Path Tracing. With 88M added parameters (approximately 2%) on Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking, our model achieves 66.43% and 72.50% accuracy, respectively, surpassing the evaluated GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro baselines. Controlled interventions show that changing selected visual content affects task accuracy and can redirect subsequent visual selection even when intervening text is held fixed. These findings show that native visual states can function as intermediate reasoning material and point toward reusable scaffolds for additional modalities.

papers.abstract: Vision-language navigation is moving into photorealistic, physically simulated scenes, where the leading zero-shot agents put a vision-language model in the control loop to choose every move and stop. Robots favour small models, whose abilities are uneven: Qwen3-VL-4B can judge whether a single view looks like the goal, but its route reasoning is at chance, its distance estimates nearly constant, its stop votes unreliable. Our agent therefore asks it two perceptual questions per step, which direction looks like the goal and whether the view justifies stopping, plus one gated frontier query on route-bearing instructions, and treats the answers as evidence, not actions: a route-blind semantic field over a bird's-eye map accumulates the directional scores through a tempered update, a skeleton graph supplies frontiers and geodesic distances, and a two-stage terminator turns stop votes into termini through a trail-consistency gate and a budget-forced return. With every baseline re-run in one installation at one budget, the agent exceeds all four zero-shot baselines of the VLNVerse subset in mean success on both granularities, though the paired interval against the strongest coarse-grained baseline includes zero. Termination is the dominant lever in ablation, thirteen attempts to give the model more of the navigation establish no reliable gain, and the agent runs on a Unitree Go2 quadruped with off-board inference. Code, per-episode logs and a robot video will be released at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/structure-over-reasoning-PAGE.

papers.abstract: Fine-tuning language models on consumer GPUs is constrained by computation and memory. Although LoRA reduces trainable parameters and optimizer state, frozen projections remain expensive, and activations retained for backward can dominate memory usage. We present PACT, a LoRA fine-tuning system that accelerates frozen projections with native NVFP4 GEMMs while reducing quantization and dequantization overhead and limiting quantization error. To reduce activation memory, PACT reuses quantized RMSNorm outputs and saves gate/up activations in NVFP4 for backward. To limit numerical error, it preserves BF16 inputs for forward nonlinear operations and calibrates frozen weights offline using GPTQ adapted to NVFP4 scales and quantized activations. Fused nonlinear kernels and cached forward and backward weight layouts reduce quantization and dequantization overhead. Evaluations across multiple models and tasks on a 16\,GB RTX~5080 show lower memory usage and faster LoRA fine-tuning with competitive accuracy, enabling model adaptation on resource-constrained consumer hardware.

analysis.key_results: 在 16GB RTX 5080 上多模型多任务评估显示更低内存占用、更快的 LoRA 微调速度和有竞争力的精度。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出 PACT 系统，通过 NVFP4 原生 GEMM 加速 LoRA 微调中的冻结投影，减少量化/反量化开销并限制量化误差，同时降低激活内存。
analysis.method: 复用量化后的 RMSNorm 输出，以 NVFP4 保存 gate/up 激活用于反向；前向非线性操作保留 BF16 输入；使用适配 NVFP4 尺度与量化激活的 GPTQ 离线校准冻结权重；采用融合非线性核及缓存前后向权重布局。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: PACT 提出一种利用 NVFP4 数据流的 LoRA 微调系统，可在消费级 GPU 上同时降低内存占用并加速冻结投影计算。
analysis.relation_to_vla_wam: 本文专注于量化方法在 LoRA 微调中的效率优化，未直接涉及 VLA、WAM 或机器人动作-世界建模；但其量化与内存优化技术对资源受限环境下的模型适配具有通用参考价值。

papers.abstract: Flow-matching vision-language-action (VLA) models generate an action chunk by iteratively denoising Gaussian noise, but typically execute only a short prefix before replanning with updated observations. Under this receding-horizon paradigm, the unexecuted remainder---the action tail---is discarded, and the next chunk is regenerated from fresh noise. We show that this discarded tail retains transferable denoising progress: action-tail initialization can match or outperform a native 10-step Gaussian baseline using fewer denoising steps. However, the optimal denoising budget varies substantially across samples, indicating that tail reuse should be adapted to the updated environment. Based on this observation, we introduce VLA-Rolling, a lightweight inference framework that reuses action tails through three stages: action-tail inheritance, per-action confidence estimation, and confidence-guided refinement through renoising and denoising budget allocation, while the underlying VLA remains frozen. Across $\pi_{0.5}$, SmolVLA, X-VLA, and MolmoAct2 on LIBERO, MetaWorld, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin 2.0, VLA-Rolling reduces action-chunk inference cost in all 16 model--benchmark pairs, achieving up to a $1.48\times$ speedup, while improving success rate in 14 pairs by up to $15.08$ percentage points. These results show that action tails are not merely discarded predictions, but reusable intermediate states that enable more efficient and accurate VLA inference. These results demonstrate that the action tail can support the generation of better actions with fewer denoising steps. Our project is available at https://chenbao123ww.github.io/VLA-Rolling/.

analysis.key_results: 在LIBERO、MetaWorld、LIBERO-Plus和RoboTwin 2.0上的π0.5、SmolVLA、X-VLA和MolmoAct2共16对模型-基准测试中，所有16对均降低了动作块推理成本，最高加速1.48倍；14对成功率提升，最高提升15.08个百分点。
analysis.main_contribution: 证明了VLA动作尾部包含可迁移的去噪进展，并提出VLA-Rolling框架，通过动作尾部继承、逐动作置信度估计和置信度引导的重噪与去噪预算分配，实现更高效且更准确的VLA推理。
analysis.method: VLA-Rolling框架：动作尾部继承、逐动作置信度估计、基于置信度的重噪与去噪预算分配；底层VLA模型保持冻结。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 提出VLA-Rolling推理框架，通过复用VLA模型在滚动规划中丢弃的动作尾部作为去噪起点，结合置信度估计与自适应细化，在冻结模型的情况下同时降低推理成本并提升成功率。

papers.abstract: As LLM adoption surges, scaling model serving requires unlocking stranded GPU capacity alongside deploying more GPUs. Speculative decoding brings two models into the serving process: a small draft model proposes tokens that a larger target model verifies. Yet compiling these models individually leaves their shared execution outside the compiler's optimization boundary. We introduce CONJUGATE COMPILATION, which reframes speculative decoding as a cross-model compilation problem and jointly optimizes the draft and target models within their shared execution rather than treating each in isolation. Our key insight is that cross-model compilation should be informed by the measured performance of the co-located shared execution it produces: an optimization that improves a kernel in isolation need not improve the models when they execute together. To expand cross-model opportunities, we devise operand layouts that interleave blocks from both models within common tiles, co-locating GEMM and non-GEMM work while preserving their mathematics. We realize CONJUGATE COMPILATION through a self-improving agentic search system in which an LLM edits cross-model optimization plans using the compiler and GPU execution as its environment. Each proposed plan is compiled and evaluated through its co-located shared execution, whose measured score, together with kernel-level verdicts and compiler feedback, informs subsequent proposals, while Monte Carlo tree search accumulates rewards to guide exploration. Across six single-GPU speculative-decoding configurations on NVIDIA B300 and RTX 5090 GPUs, CONJUGATE COMPILATION achieves a geometric-mean per-round speedup of 1.37x over conventional execution. Interleaved kernels raise this speedup to 1.45x, reaching 1.59x in the best case. CONJUGATE COMPILATION also improves GPU utilization on average by 1.46x on RTX 5090 and 1.50x on B300.

analysis.key_results: 在NVIDIA B300和RTX 5090 GPU上的六种单GPU推测解码配置中，共轭编译实现几何平均每轮加速1.37倍；交错内核将加速提升至1.45倍，最佳情况1.59倍；GPU利用率平均提升1.46倍（RTX 5090）和1.50倍（B300）。

papers.abstract: The throughput gains of speculative decoding depend on the trade-off between acceptance length and execution latency. We ask when additional acceptance is worth the cost of obtaining it. We establish a comparison protocol spanning training, inference, and evaluation, remeasuring released checkpoints and retraining six drafter recipes on shared target-generated data across ten benchmarks and two target models. Alignment changes the picture: gaps that appear large in published comparisons shrink substantially under shared training and inference conditions. This narrowing motivates two deeper questions: how is acceptance improved at different costs, and when do these gains improve throughput? We find that acceptance can be improved through nearly free objective and context changes or more expensive token-to-token conditioning. DCore illustrates the former route as a strong baseline with little additional measured drafting overhead. The payoff is conditional: task uncertainty and serving conditions affect acceptance returns, execution costs, and the preferred drafter and budget. These findings inform future drafter design and deployment choices.

analysis.key_results: 对齐后，已发布比较中的大差距显著缩小；接受率可通过近乎免费的目标和上下文改变或更昂贵的令牌到令牌条件化改善；DCore作为低成本高接受率的强基线；接受率收益取决于任务不确定性和服务条件。
analysis.main_contribution: 建立一个涵盖训练、推理和评估的比较协议，在十个基准和两个目标模型上重新测量已发布检查点并重训六种草稿器，发现对齐后差距缩小，并揭示了接受率提升的不同成本途径及其条件性收益。
analysis.method: 在共享目标生成数据上重训六种草稿器配方，并在十个基准和两个目标模型上进行受控比较；分析接受率改进的低成本（目标与上下文改变）和高成本（令牌到令牌条件化）途径。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 通过受控实验研究投机解码中接受长度与执行延迟之间的权衡，重新测量已发布检查点并在共享条件下重训多种草稿器，以回答何时更高的接受率能转化为吞吐量提升。

papers.abstract: Video models provide rich priors for generalizable robotic manipulation, but plausible visual futures are not always executable. We introduce DreamCan, a hierarchical policy that grounds video models through sparse visual planning: a high-level planner adapted from a pre-trained video model and a low-level visuomotor policy. Rather than predicting dense trajectories, the high-level planner generates sparse visual subgoals that balance reachability and task utility. From offline, action-free robot videos, we estimate these quantities and use dynamic programming to select subgoal sequences without manual annotations. The resulting subgoals are more reliably attained than uniformly spaced alternatives, and the full system outperforms language, dense-video, and uniform-subgoal planners, reaching high planning success rates on Language-Table tasks and 91.2% success on LIBERO-Long with a 0.1B-parameter low-level policy. Additional suboptimal videos and test-time compute further improve success. The system also performs challenging real-world bimanual tasks, including box folding and packing with unseen object combinations. More results are available at https://dreamcan.github.io/.

analysis.key_results: 在Language-Table任务上达到高规划成功率，在LIBERO-Long上以0.1B参数的低层策略实现91.2%成功率；增加次优视频和测试时计算可进一步提升成功率；在真实世界双手操作任务（如叠箱子和打包未见物体组合）中也能有效执行。
analysis.main_contribution: 引入了一种新的分层策略，通过稀疏视觉规划将视频模型的能力接地到可执行的机器人操作中，无需手动标注即可从离线无动作视频数据中自动选择子目标序列。
analysis.method: 使用从预训练视频模型适配的高层规划器生成稀疏视觉子目标，并通过动态规划基于可达性和任务效用选择子目标序列；低层采用视觉运动策略执行。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 提出DreamCan，一种利用预训练视频模型生成稀疏视觉子目标并进行分层规划的机器人操作策略，以提升任务可执行性和泛化性。

papers.abstract: We study quantization for inner-product estimation when storage and reading have separate budgets. In the static bit-probe model [Yao, 1981], an encoder stores $w$ bits about $x$ before seeing a query $y$, and a reader probes at most $r<w$ bits to estimate $x^\top y$. Both vectors lie in the $d$-dimensional Euclidean unit ball. Protocols may be randomized, and computation is unrestricted. Performance is measured by $d$ times the worst-case mean-squared error over $x,y$, averaged over protocol randomness. First, we show that query-independent reading cannot benefit from extra storage. Any such reader is equivalent to fully reading an $r$-bit message, even when later reads depend on previously returned bits. At fixed positive rates $W=w/d$ and $R=r/d$, the normalized minimax error converges to $1/(4^R-1)$, independent of $W$. The upper bound was already known [Ordentlich and Polyanskiy, 2025]. We prove the matching lower bound for arbitrary scalar decoders, extending the result for unbiased compressors [Safaryan et al., 2020]. Then, we show that query-dependent reading makes extra storage useful. We construct a two-batch protocol using Gaussian projections and random thresholds, with asymptotic normalized error at most $(\pi+o(1))/[4R\log(W/R)]$ as $W/R\to\infty$. At fixed $R$, this error vanishes as storage grows, giving an unbounded advantage over query-independent reading. We also prove a finite-dimensional lower bound for arbitrary encoders, decoders, and fully branching readers. In the doubly sparse regime $W/R\to\infty$ and $R\log(W/R)\to0$, it gives normalized error at least $(1-o(1))/[2R\log(W/R)]$. Thus, our protocol is optimal within a factor of $\pi/2$ in the leading constant.

analysis.key_results: 在查询独立读取下，归一化极小极大误差收敛于1/(4^R-1)，与存储量W无关；在查询依赖读取下，构造的两批协议渐近归一化误差至多为(π+o(1))/[4R log(W/R)]，且当W/R→∞时误差趋于0，优于查询独立读取；此外，给出了有限维下界(1-o(1))/[2R log(W/R)]，表明该协议在领先常数上至多相差π/2。
analysis.main_contribution: 证明了查询依赖读取可以利用额外存储显著降低量化内积估计的误差，并构造了一个两批协议，其误差随存储增长而消失，而查询独立读取则无法从额外存储中获益。
analysis.method: 采用静态位探针模型，构造了基于高斯投影和随机阈值的两批协议，并利用了极小极大分析和信息论工具。

papers.abstract: Lifelong robot learning requires acquiring new tasks sequentially without forgetting earlier ones. With large pre-trained vision-language-action (VLA) backbones, adapter-based methods effectively mitigate this challenge. However, their task-specific adapters and selection modules accumulate with the task stream, creating a scalability challenge in on-disk storage and deployment cost under fixed onboard resource budgets. We propose SARAM, a lifelong learning framework that limits storage growth while keeping GPU memory and per-step inference cost independent of the task stream length. For each new task, SARAM reuses frozen adapters from previous tasks and introduces new adapters only at sparsely selected layers, with a duplication penalty encouraging them to capture information not already represented by the adapter library. At deployment, a compact signature derived from backbone activation statistics identifies the task once per episode, and the corresponding task update is merged into the backbone, leaving only the backbone in the control loop. Across four LIBERO suites, SARAM matches or exceeds adapter-based baselines while adding up to 4.5x less on-disk state per task. GPU memory usage and control frequency remain comparable to those of the backbone as the task stream grows. Experiments on a real UR5 arm with a different backbone further demonstrate retention throughout a sequential task stream.

analysis.key_results: 在四个LIBERO套件上，SARAM与基于适配器的基线相比性能相当或更优，每个任务的磁盘状态增加最多减少4.5倍；GPU内存使用和控制频率随任务流增长保持与骨干网络相当。在真实UR5机械臂上验证了不同骨干下的保留能力。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出SARAM框架，在终身机器人学习中限制存储增长，同时保持GPU内存和每步推理成本与任务流长度无关。
analysis.method: 对每个新任务，复用之前任务的冻结适配器，仅在稀疏选择的层引入新适配器，并施加复制惩罚以促进捕获适配器库中未表示的信息；部署时基于骨干激活统计的紧凑签名每个回合识别任务，并将相应任务更新合并回骨干网络。

papers.abstract: Can a better robot policy become harder to monitor? We study a fixed vision-language model (VLM) that judges success while a policy improves. In a controlled 20-seed tray-placement experiment, training selects only simulator-verified successes. Success rises from 66.8% to 97.0%, and accepted hover failures fall from 5.0% to 0.9% of executions. Yet the judge accepts 50.0% of remaining hovers, versus 31.1% under untrained sampling. These residual failures more often lie below the tray rim, which can conceal the gap beneath a grasped cube. A separate boundary probe accepts 148/160 below-rim hovers and 0/160 above-rim hovers. We call this change in conditional monitoring sensitivity coverage shift: learning changes which failures reach a fixed judge. A broader diagnosis covers nine judges and 1,392 stimuli. Judge-filtered experiments across eight settings further show heterogeneous effects of state-dependent acceptance. The results distinguish task improvement from failure detectability and motivate reporting absolute misses, conditional misses, and audit coverage together.

analysis.key_results: 策略成功率从66.8%提升到97.0%，接受的悬停失败比例从5.0%降至0.9%，但VLM对剩余悬停失败的接受率从31.1%升至50.0%；边界探针接受148/160个边缘下方悬停和0/160个边缘上方悬停。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出并实证分析了“覆盖偏移”（coverage shift）现象：当机器人策略在学习过程中提升时，剩余失败样本的条件分布发生变化，导致固定VLM判断器的监测敏感性改变。
analysis.method: 在受控托盘放置实验中，使用固定VLM作为成功判断器，比较训练前后策略的失败样本被VLM接受的比例，并通过边界探针实验区分不同失败模式（如托盘边缘下方悬停）的检测差异。

papers.abstract: Existing Multi-token prediction (MTP) methods are auxiliary by design: the multi-horizon loss mostly trains modules attached to the backbone, and each added horizon costs another module and another pass. We propose Efficient Causal Self-Recursion (ECHO), which removes both costs. The backbone's own final layer predicts every horizon, so the supervision lands on the parameters that generate the next token, and Dynamic Depth Sampling (DDS) keeps deeper horizons affordable by drawing the training depth with probabilities that decay along depth. Future prediction thus becomes part of the autoregressive objective rather than a task attached to it, and the gains follow on both sides of it. In pretraining, added depth converts into downstream accuracy where auxiliary modules saturate, concentrating on reasoning and code at half the MTP training overhead of training every depth. At inference, the pretrained model is its own drafter: it drafts beyond the depth it was trained for, and keeps its draft-target alignment on the open-ended, high-entropy generation where post-hoc drafters lose theirs. The advantage survives a doubled token budget, a repeated pretraining run, and supervised finetuning.

analysis.key_results: 在预训练中，增加深度转化为下游精度提升，相比训练所有深度仅需一半的训练开销；在推理中，预训练模型可自起草超出训练深度的令牌，并在开放式高熵生成中保持草稿与目标对齐。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出高效因果自递归（ECHO）方法，通过骨干网络自身最终层预测所有前瞻步长，避免额外模块和多次前向传递，将未来预测纳入自回归目标而非附加任务。
analysis.method: 骨干网络最终层自递归预测多步；动态深度采样（DDS）以随深度衰减的概率采样训练深度，保持深层预测可负担。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 提出高效因果自递归方法，使骨干网络自递归预测多步令牌，减少多令牌预测的训练与推理开销。

papers.abstract: The scan-then-revisit workflow of upper gastrointestinal endoscopy requires bringing a previously observed suspicious region back into view for closer inspection. Acquiring such targets requires translating anatomical and appearance descriptions into camera motions from partial observations of a confined, deformable environment. We present EndoVLA-OOV, a language-conditioned vision-language-action policy for out-of-view target acquisition in robotic endoscopy. The policy adapts a pretrained backbone to continuous two-degree-of-freedom distal bending commands and combines initial, intermediate, and current images to guide search. To support policy learning, we provide an open-source VLA dataset containing 1,050 episodes across six tasks and approximately 262k observation-action pairs. Physical evaluation spans wet-lens and low-light conditions, two unseen stomach phantoms, and cross-embodiment transfer to an unseen ex-vivo environment. In the cross-embodiment evaluation, the full-data policy achieves 93.3% target acquisition success (28/30). In a controlled training-data comparison, expanding the corpus from 312 to 1,050 episodes increases acquisition success from 40.0% to 90.0% under the same model, training, and test configuration. Instruction and observation interventions further support the use of language and temporal context in the evaluated acquisition tasks. These results support language-guided endoscopic revisitation across the evaluated environments and robot embodiments and demonstrate the benefit of expanded task-specific demonstrations.

papers.abstract: Discrete diffusion language models (dLLMs) offer an attractive alternative to autoregressive generation by updating multiple tokens in parallel, but their inference efficiency is still limited by the cost of safely committing tentative predictions. In particular, speculative decoding for dLLMs is challenging because speculative tokens within the same diffusion block may depend on one another, making aggressive acceptance prone to error propagation and strict verification computationally expensive. We present PV-Decoding, a confidence-driven speculative decoding framework with progressive verification for block diffusion inference. PV-Decoding partitions masked positions into directly decoded tokens, speculative tokens, and unresolved tokens using two confidence thresholds, and then verifies speculative tokens with progressively stronger policies, including single-batch, dual-batch, and multi-batch verification. This design exposes a practical accuracy--efficiency trade-off: weaker verification minimizes overhead, whereas stronger verification improves acceptance precision and robustness. Experiments on three diffusion language models across GSM8K, MBPP, and HumanEval show that PV-Decoding reduces sequential model forward passes (MFPs) by 8%--37% relative to confidence-based decoding, while keeping the largest observed accuracy drop to 1.3%. On Dream-7B-Instruct/GSM8K, PV-Decoding (1-batch) and PV-Decoding (2-batch) improve throughput by 7.0%--13.6% under the same hardware budget, whereas PV-Decoding (multi-batch) is slower under the current runtime. These results suggest that confidence-guided speculation with structured verification is a practical path toward efficient and reliable dLLM inference.

analysis.key_results: 在三个扩散语言模型（GSM8K、MBPP、HumanEval）上相对于置信度解码减少顺序前向传递8%–37%，最大准确度下降1.3%；在 Dream-7B-Instruct/GSM8K 上，1批和2批验证吞吐量提升7.0%–13.6%，多批验证在当前实现下较慢。

papers.abstract: Spatial understanding is essential for robots to perceive their surrounding environments and execute actions. Existing approaches typically encode 3D awareness into vision-language-action (VLA) models by directly aligning their representations with pre-trained 3D foundation models. However, we observe that such direct geometric feature alignment essentially exploits 3D foundation priors as a form of low-rank regularization in the feature space, resulting in severe rank collapse of the pre-trained VLA representations. In contrast, we shift the focus from enforcing point-wise equality to aligning pair-wise relationships. We propose a representation-alignment method that enables the injection of 3D spatial awareness without compromising the model's original expressivity. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks, our new spatial reasoning benchmark, and real-world manipulation scenarios demonstrate that our approach effectively incorporates 3D spatial representations into VLA reasoning, achieving robust performance and enhanced spatial awareness across diverse manipulation tasks.

analysis.method: 将3D空间先验通过成对关系对齐注入VLA表征，而非逐点几何特征对齐。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 提出用成对关系对齐替代逐点对齐，将3D空间意识注入VLA模型，避免预训练表征的秩坍缩。

papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have achieved remarkable progress in 2D visual understanding tasks, yet the passive view-centric perception paradigm limits their capacity for 3D spatial reasoning. Such reasoning often requires actively acquiring spatial evidence beyond the currently visible views, such as camera poses and cross-view spatial relationships, to infer 3D relationships that are not explicitly represented in 2D images. However, existing methods either lack active exploration or merely provide additional views during inference, without explicitly acquiring such spatial evidence beyond 2D images. In this paper, we propose View-to-World (V2W), an active exploration framework that enables VLMs to actively explore 3D worlds and lifts VLMs from passive view-centric perception to active world-centric spatial reasoning. Given a spatial reasoning task with multi-view images, V2W first reconstructs an explicit 3D world with geometry, camera poses, and language-grounded semantics, and exposes it to VLMs through visual and linguistic interfaces. Through multi-turn interaction with these interfaces, VLMs iteratively acquire spatial evidence from the constructed 3D world, enabling active world-centric spatial reasoning. V2W can be integrated with existing VLMs in a training-free manner and can be further enhanced by optimizing the exploration policy via reinforcement learning. Experiments on spatial mental modeling benchmarks demonstrate that V2W substantially improves VLM baselines in the training-free setting and achieves state-of-the-art performance with the learned exploration policy, highlighting the importance of active exploration for spatial intelligence. Project page: \url{https://fangzhou2000.github.io/projects/v2w}.

papers.abstract: Digital medicine now captures data that traces individual health trajectories and reveals population health dynamics through electronic health records, claims, remote monitoring, wearable devices, mobile devices, social sensing data, medical images, etc. But much of its modeling still centers on task-specific, outcome-specific, and prediction-specific estimation. The next frontier is not simply better prediction, but action in an evolving health world shaped by multiple decision-makers, heterogeneous populations, resource constraints, and feedback in care delivery. This is why digital medicine now needs world models: not only to estimate what will happen, but to represent how actions change what can happen next -- whom to prioritize, how to allocate scarce resources, how to adapt care across subgroups, and how interventions reshape future health trajectories and population dynamics. We call such a model population health world model (PHWM): a more foundational representation of an evolving health world in which health states, individual trajectories, population health dynamics, interventions, constraints, and feedback are intrinsically coupled. Building a PHWM endows three unmet structural gaps in current digital medicine: dynamic health-state modeling, population-level intervention intelligence, and validation, equity, and governance for action-oriented use. We argue that addressing these gaps requires three minimal capabilities: representation learning under action-dependent observation, multi-scale intervention intelligence, and validation with explicit decision boundaries, while highlighting the importance of social, contextual, and public-health sensing data for action-oriented digital medicine.

figures.caption: Overview of Population Health World Model: Observed health signals—including electronic health records, claims, wearable and remote-monitoring data, patient-reported outcomes, and social or contextual signals—feed into a population health world model that distinguishes latent health state from recorded observations. The model represents intervention space, transition dynamics, uncertainty, and hierarchy across levels and time scales, linking patient-level health trajectories to subgroup patterns and population health dynamics. Interventions and real-world constraints jointly shape intervention-conditioned dynamics, which in turn support action-oriented outputs such as prioritization, scenario analysis, coverage planning, and resource allocation. Validation and governance form an integrated layer spanning the framework, emphasizing predictive validity, intervention sensitivity, counterfactual plausibility, robustness under shift, usefulness, and equity.

figures.caption: Structural Gaps and Minimal Required Capabilities in Population Health World Model. Current digital medicine models rely on assumptions that observed features approximate health state, that decisions can be modeled at the patient level, and that evaluation under observed processes is sufficient. These assumptions lead to three structural gaps: (1) representational challenges arising from latent state being confounded with intervention-dependent observations, (2) multi-scale coupling challenges due to interactions across individuals, subgroups, and populations under shared constraints, and (3) validation challenges under intervention, feedback, and distribution shift. Addressing these gaps requires minimal capabilities rather than optional directions: representation learning under action-dependent observation, multi-scale intervention intelligence, and validation frameworks with explicit decision boundaries. These priorities correspond to core problem classes in artificial intelligence, including partially observable modeling, multi-agent and hierarchical systems, and off-policy and uncertainty-aware evaluation.

papers.abstract: We introduce Muse Glimmer, an open-source 30B parameter causal language model with perception encoder, purpose-built for autonomous agentic tasks on consumer hardware. Muse Glimmer integrates multi-step reasoning, reliable tool use and failure recovery into a single model that runs locally on consumer devices without requiring cloud infrastructure. The model accepts text and image inputs and produces text outputs, was trained on data from over a hundred languages, and is quantized to approximately 4-bit precision for efficient single-GPU inference. Muse Glimmer achieves state-of-the-art performance for its size class on agentic benchmarks, setting a new standard compared to the models of its size: Gemma4-31B and Qwen3.6-27B on tool use, multi-step planning, and agentic task completion. We release the model under the Apache 2.0 license to foster open-source development of capable, safe, local AI agents.

papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models offer a promising paradigm for autonomous driving. However, the massive parameter scale of VLAs strains onboard computational resources during real-time inference. This directly increases energy consumption and limits vehicle battery range, making it critical to minimize computational overhead without compromising driving capability and explainability. Current research on efficient VLA-based driving focuses on sequential adaptation (\textit{e.g.}, Chain-of-Thought and token adjustment), leaving structural adaptation underexplored despite parameter redundancy across dynamic driving scenes. To address this gap, we propose Scene-Adaptive VLA, an efficient framework leveraging dynamic layer routing to adjust active parameters based on real-time scenes. Inspired by the temporal continuity of scenes and model predictive uncertainty, our approach characterizes model-perceived scene complexity via frame-level temporal scene variations and decision deviations. To uncover latent scene-to-parameter correspondences, we encode this characterization into scene-aware tokens, alongside two specialized queries. A budget-conditioned layer routing mechanism evaluates these refined queries to allocate a budget that determines the active parameter ratio and subsequently selects appropriate layer combinations. The entire framework is optimized end-to-end. Extensive evaluations on the Bench2Drive benchmark show that when adapted to a state-of-the-art VLA model, our approach significantly reduces inference-time computational overhead by 53.5\% with negligible degradation in driving and language capabilities. Code is available at https:github.com/yang-luvu/Scene-Adaptive-VLA.

papers.abstract: LIBERO has emerged as a widely adopted benchmark for evaluating robotic manipulation policies. However, strong performance on LIBERO does not necessarily indicate robust embodied capabilities, as models may exploit benchmark-specific regularities rather than generalize to diverse operating conditions. In this work, we introduce LIBERO-Pro2.0, a comprehensive benchmark for systematically evaluating the robustness of embodied foundation models under distribution shifts. LIBERO-Pro2.0 encompasses 22 static perturbations and 20 runtime interventions across six dimensions: Condition, Environment, Observation, Execution, Robot State Configuration, and Language, yielding 1,648 validated shifted task instances. To support robustness-oriented learning, we further collect 39,390 training trajectories through model-generated and human demonstrations. All shifted task instances undergo six rounds of iterative human review and correction to ensure physical plausibility and task validity. We evaluate 17 representative robot policies spanning vision-language-action models, world-action models, and robustness-oriented policies. Our results reveal substantial robustness gaps across all evaluated paradigms: under runtime distribution shifts, the evaluated models exhibit an average performance drop of 26.5 percentage points, with individual drops reaching 32.5 points. These findings highlight the gap between nominal benchmark performance and robustness under distribution shifts, underscoring the need for systematic robustness evaluation of embodied foundation models.

papers.abstract: Frozen Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies cannot incorporate previously encountered failures without updating the underlying model. We present retrieval-triggered projection correction (RTPC), an auditable external-memory wrapper for frozen OpenVLA policies that retrieves stress-collected local-depth records and applies translation-only projection correction while keeping rotation and gripper commands unchanged. RTPC is evaluated on CALVIN single-task manipulation using primary and independent replication cohorts. In the primary evaluation, RTPC reduced a depth-based near-collision or stall proxy event rate without changing task-success count. However, this reduction was not reproduced in the independent replication, and retrieved correction directions were not distinguishable from random same-family directions. Analysis identifies endpoint coupling, batch sensitivity, and the lack of a trigger-matched memory-free baseline as limitations for attributing effects to retrieval-based correction. These findings do not establish physical safety improvement or memory-specific benefits, but provide an empirical evaluation and failure analysis of retrieval-conditioned intervention for frozen VLA policies.

analysis.limitations: 端点耦合、批次敏感性以及缺乏触发匹配的无记忆基线，限制了对检索式校正效应的归因；研究未能确立物理安全改进或记忆特异性益处。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出检索触发投影校正（RTPC），一种可审计的外部记忆包装器，通过检索压力采集的局部深度记录并对冻结 OpenVLA 策略进行仅平移的投影校正，并以严格的双队列复现实验对其进行评估和失败分析。

papers.abstract: Enabling humanoid robots to participate effectively in social interactions is important for their integration into human-centered environments. Existing methods, however, typically map pre-generated speech directly to continuous motion trajectories but have limited awareness of complex social environments and lack explicit high-level semantic action planning. We introduce SocialCoAct, a unified agent-centered framework for VLM-based egocentric social co-action. We formulate egocentric social co-action as an end-to-end agent task and develop SocialCoAct-Agent, which transforms egocentric observations and dialogue history into verbal responses and atomic action sequences, aligns each action with its corresponding utterance span, and executes the resulting behaviors in MuJoCo and on a physical humanoid robot. To evaluate the VLM capabilities required by this task, we construct SocialCoAct-Bench from continuous egocentric recordings of natural multi-party interactions. The benchmark comprises 423 human-verified multiple-choice questions across three subtasks: Long Episode Understanding (LEU), Speaker Intention Understanding (SIU), and Coordinated Action Planning (CAP). Across a diverse set of closed-source and open-weight VLMs, including general and egocentric models, the highest overall accuracy is 77.54%, while accuracy on the hard subset reaches only 46.51%. Extended reasoning improves Qwen3-VL-2B and Qwen3-VL-4B by 19.62 and 17.02 percentage points, respectively, but reduces inference throughput by 53.6$\times$ and 20.2$\times$. Visual-input ablations further show that the benefits of visual context vary across models. SocialCoAct provides a foundation for developing and evaluating VLM-based humanoid agents that coordinate context-aware speech and action in complex social interactions. The codebase and benchmark will be made publicly available upon publication.

papers.abstract: Reliable long-horizon prediction remains a central challenge for embodied world models. Although recent generative models can synthesize visually plausible action-conditioned futures, their latent dynamics are typically learned through unconstrained transition modules, which may gradually deviate from coherent physical evolution as predictions are recursively rolled forward. We investigate whether explicitly structuring latent state evolution can improve the stability and utility of such imagined trajectories. To this end, we introduce HWM, a structured dynamics framework that represents backbone latents in a learned phase space consisting of generalized coordinates and momenta. Future states are propagated through dissipative Hamiltonian dynamics and mapped back to the original latent representation through a learnable inverse interface. The resulting formulation can be integrated into existing world-model architectures without redesigning their perception or decoding components, while multi-step transition supervision encourages the structured rollout to remain aligned with the latent trajectories induced by real observations. Controlled simulation experiments show that HWM produces more accurate estimates of velocity, acceleration, and jerk and substantially reduces long-horizon energy drift relative to unstructured latent dynamics. We further evaluate the approach across three distinct embodied world-model settings, covering single-arm multi-view prediction with Ctrl-World, dual-arm single-view prediction with EVAC, and task-oriented single-arm prediction with Cosmos-Predict2.5-2B. On RoboCasa, incorporating HWM into Cosmos-Predict2.5-2B yields a 2.7% relative improvement in task success. On real-world AgiBot World trajectories, it improves nDTW by 9.7% with Ctrl-World and Logic by 8.4% with EVAC.

papers.abstract: Conformal prediction (CP) is a post-hoc calibration method that returns prediction sets with distribution-free coverage guarantees, and the size of the output set is often interpreted as a notion of uncertainty. We show that the difference in set size between full and split CP is directly connected to Bayesian posterior variance, which is the epistemic uncertainty of the model. Essentially, this difference in set size is an aggregation of two opposite effects: (1) better model accuracy and therefore smaller set size achieved by training over extra calibration points, and (2) the "formability" of the model at test point towards every possible label. The latter effect vanishes with stronger models or more calibration data (as epistemic uncertainty is known for that behavior). It turns out that the model's formability itself (without the quantization effect of prediction sets, and through estimating the posterior variance) is a useful tool to quantify the epistemic uncertainty. In our empirical evaluation it performs on par with the state of the art in many setups.

papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies must ground language instructions in the right objects, contact points, and target locations for reliable manipulation. Human gaze provides a natural signal for this grounding, but existing robot datasets rarely pair real human gaze with the multi-camera observations used by modern policies. We introduce GazeAct, a gaze-equipped real-robot manipulation dataset and training framework for multi-view VLA policies. Using screen-based teleoperation, we record gaze directly on the robot camera feed viewed by the operator, yielding 12000 demonstrations across 40 tasks and five domains with 300 Hz gaze synchronized with images, proprioception, and actions. We transfer gaze from the operator-selected view to the remaining synchronized cameras, producing spatially consistent targets across the policy's visual inputs. We then use these gaze-derived targets to regularize language-conditioned visual attention during training while keeping inference gaze-free. Across 18 real-world tasks, our method improves average success from 48.1% to 58.6%, with gains up to 25 percentage points. Ablations show that gaze works best as soft supervision and that real human gaze provides stronger attention targets than generic attention-shaping priors. The gains transfer to LIBERO-Spatial (57.9% to 69.6%) and different VLA backbones.These results show that gaze collected in the robot observation space can provide effective training-time targets for improving visual grounding in VLA manipulation.

papers.abstract: Reverse target fishing identifies protein targets for a query molecule and is central to drug discovery and repurposing. Discriminative approaches adapted from virtual screening face sparse, long-tailed associations and missing-not-at-random measurements: treating unrecorded pairs as negatives can suppress genuine targets. We reformulate the task as generative retrieval and introduce GenFish. Residual vector quantization converts frozen protein language model features into shared semantic identifiers. Given a molecular fingerprint, GenFish autoregressively models codes conditioned on the query and preceding code, ranking proteins by identifier likelihood without explicitly labeling unrecorded pairs as negatives. We introduce ProTargetBench, the first proteome-scale benchmark for reverse target fishing to jointly support measured-panel discrimination and full-catalogue recovery of experimentally recorded positives. Covering 20,431 UniProt-reviewed human proteins, it integrates curated bioactivity evidence and distinguishes experimental inactivity from unmeasured associations. On 198 held-out molecules, GenFish achieves higher mean performance across all three full-catalogue retrieval metrics than four discriminative neural baselines and three non-neural baselines, including ligand-based methods. A controlled positive-hiding experiment shows that targeted removal of false-negative competition improves contrastive retrieval beyond matched random masking; GenFish remains stronger under the same incomplete supervision. Pfam alignment indicates that the semantic identifiers capture biologically meaningful relationships among proteins. These results establish generative retrieval as a principled paradigm for reverse target fishing under incomplete bioactivity records.

analysis.key_results: 在198个留存分子上，GenFish在全部三个全目录检索指标上平均性能优于四个判别式神经基线和三个非神经基线；受控正例隐藏实验显示其优于匹配随机掩码；Pfam比对表明语义标识符捕获了生物学上有意义的蛋白质关系。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出GenFish模型，将反向靶点识别重构为生成式检索任务，并引入首个蛋白质组规模基准ProTargetBench。
analysis.method: 利用残差向量量化将冻结的蛋白质语言模型特征转换为共享语义标识符，再基于分子指纹自回归地建模这些标识符的条件概率来排序蛋白质。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: GenFish通过残差向量量化将蛋白质语言模型特征转换为语义标识符，在ProTargetBench上以生成式检索方式提升反向靶点发现性能。

papers.abstract: GUI world models are increasingly used to improve action selection by predicting the consequences of candidate actions, but it is unclear how much of the resulting gain comes from prediction itself rather than from the evaluator that interprets those predictions. We study this attribution problem through controlled interventions on GUI action selection. With candidates and predictions held fixed, lookahead gains can change with how the prediction is presented to the evaluator, so end-to-end gains cannot be attributed to prediction alone. We then introduce Direct Action Ranking (DAR), which learns from reference actions to score candidates without generating future screens, and compare it with a prediction-augmented variant under matched supervision. Predicted successors add no detectable ranking signal once evaluation is learned directly. Without retraining, DAR improves AndroidWorld task success by 5.8--16.4 points across three proposers, outperforms world-model lookahead, and transfers zero-shot to unseen apps, where every prediction-conditioned configuration falls below proposer confidence. These results suggest that GUI world models should be evaluated by their decision value, the incremental action-selection value of their predictions beyond a strong direct evaluator, rather than by prediction fidelity or end-to-end lookahead gain alone.

papers.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model (LLM) inference by using a lightweight drafter to propose a block of tokens that the target model verifies in one parallel pass. Autoregressive drafters generate this block one token at a time, whereas block diffusion drafters such as DFlash generate it in one pass, making drafting faster. However, these diffusion drafters predict each token independently, ignoring dependencies between tokens in the block. We introduce FlashMap, a continuous flow drafter that conditions a flow map language model on the target model's hidden states and generates the whole block in one forward pass while capturing inter-token dependencies. On Qwen3-8B, FlashMap is faster than a matched DFlash baseline on every benchmark, with 7% higher average speedup and up to 6.1x lossless acceleration.

analysis.method: 使用以目标模型隐藏状态为条件的连续流草稿模型，在单次前向传播中生成整个 token 块并捕获 token 间依赖。

papers.abstract: Real-time interaction requires agents to perceive evolving environments and act under temporal constraints, yet existing evaluations of real-time streaming models focus on conversational quality and streaming perception, leaving effective action under strict temporal constraints untested. We introduce Realtime-Bench, a suite of carefully curated dynamic tasks where delayed actions directly affect success. Under Wall Clock, where environments advance according to actual inference latency, the best success rate reaches only 44% and the best Pass^3 is only 36%, demonstrating that real-time interaction remains challenging. To separate serving latency from models' real-time streaming capability, we compare Wall Clock with Paused Clock, which removes inference delays as an idealized reference, and introduce Token Clock, which advances simulated time according to generated token counts, testing temporal awareness independently of physical serving speed. We find that temporal costs limit success in evolving environments and that higher reasoning effort has mixed effects under time pressure, reflecting a trade-off between decision quality and timely execution. These findings suggest directions for improving real-time multimodal agents, including adaptive reasoning with temporal awareness and continuous perception and action.

analysis.key_results: 在Wall Clock下最佳成功率为44%，最佳Pass^3为36%；时间成本限制成功率，更高的推理努力在时间压力下效果混合。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出Realtime-Bench基准，通过Wall Clock、Paused Clock和Token Clock三种时钟协议，系统评估模型在实时交互中延迟对任务成功的影响。

papers.abstract: Robotic manipulation is inherently geometric, but what shape does the world take inside the policy that performs it? Prior work on vision-language-action (VLA) policies establishes that task-relevant variables are linearly readable from activations, yet readability certifies only that a variable is present and says nothing about the shape its values trace, which may be curved and multi-dimensional. Using controlled sweeps, natural rollouts, linear probes, and activation interventions, we build a taxonomy of seven task-relevant concepts in VLA models. We find that realized geometry is predominantly multi-dimensional and is shaped by the constraints under which the policy acts. Physical joint limits, for example, leave wrist orientation an open arc rather than a circle, and distance to the target, a single scalar, is realized in two orthogonal subspaces, a coarse ruler for the approach and a fine ruler for the grasp. The same geometries reappear in two further VLA models on real-world robot data, indicating that they are neither model-specific nor artifacts of simulation. We demonstrate how the findings are actionable by steering along the geometry a concept realizes. Overall, this work lays out an initial phenomenology of realized geometry in VLA policies and demonstrates that a concept's shape carries as much importance as its readability.

analysis.key_results: 实现的几何形状主要是多维的：例如，手腕方向形成一个开放弧线而非圆形，目标距离分别实现在两个正交子空间（接近阶段用粗尺，抓取阶段用细尺）；相同几何形状在基于真实世界机器人数据的两个VLA模型上重现。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出了VLA模型中任务相关概念神经几何的初步现象学，表明概念的几何形状与其可读性同样重要。

papers.abstract: Video generators serve as interactive worlds for exploration and simulation, yet realistic and visually appealing frames do not necessarily depict a consistent 3D world. Existing benchmarks assess selected geometric properties or use vision-language models to judge memory and consistency, leaving systematic 3D evaluation underexplored. We introduce Orbia, the first benchmark dedicated to a systematic and comprehensive evaluation of 3D consistency in interactive world models. Through controlled exploration and revisit, we organize the evaluation into three dimensions: input preservation, generated-content persistence, and 3D self-consistency. For input preservation, registered RGB-D references and annotated anchors support appearance, geometry, and spatial stability measurements. For generated-content persistence, we compare revisits to regions absent from the input image with their first generated observations to test whether models preserve what they create. For 3D self-consistency, cross-view depth and feature correspondence, regional scale agreement, and held-out Gaussian rendering test whether generated views describe the same 3D scene. Minute-long exploration and revisits further test long-term consistency. Our construction and annotation pipeline brings together public datasets, self-captured scenes, and simulation, yielding 720 instances across indoor and outdoor environments and six exploration-and-revisit protocols. Evaluation spans 27 text-, action-, and camera-conditioned models through native-interface adapters. Our Orbia benchmark provides a systematic basis for diagnosing 3D inconsistency and developing more persistent video world models.

papers.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive generation by drafting multiple tokens per step, yet feature-based drafters rely on target hidden features whose contextual emphasis may not align with the needs of subsequent draft positions. Hybrid linear attention (HLA) models maintain compact recurrent states that accumulate historical associations, offering an efficient source of complementary context for speculative drafting. We introduce ReaDy, the first speculative decoding method, to the best of our knowledge, to leverage HLA recurrent states for position-specific context retrieval during drafting. ReaDy equips each draft position with a learned query to retrieve supplementary context directly from the target's committed recurrent states. A lightweight state reader integrates this context into draft representations through residual updates, while low-rank state reads and fused operators keep additional computation and I/O overhead low. Building on DSpark's parallel backbone and sequential prediction head, ReaDy employs a lightweight two-stage adaptation strategy, with reader capacity, state sources, and residual placement examined through ablation studies. Across seven benchmarks spanning mathematics, code generation, and dialogue, ReaDy achieves an average $3.16\times$ decoding speedup over autoregressive decoding with Qwen3.8-27B on a single NVIDIA B200 GPU. It outperforms DSpark on every benchmark, improving throughput by 7.97% and acceptance length by 8.50% on average. Our code is available at https://github.com/StartLuxLabs/ReaDy.

analysis.key_results: 在涵盖数学、代码生成和对话的七个基准上，使用 Qwen3.8-27B 在单个 NVIDIA B200 GPU 上相比自回归解码平均实现 3.16 倍加速；在每个基准上均优于 DSpark，平均吞吐量提升 7.97%，接受长度提升 8.50%。

papers.abstract: Action-chunking vision-language-action (VLA) models predict sequences of future robot actions. Under fixed-horizon execution, the robot executes a fixedlength prefix of each predicted chunk before invoking the policy again, leaving the remaining predictions unused. For a given number of executed actions, short execution horizons require more policy calls. Extending the execution horizon amortizes policy inference cost over more actions. However, uniformly applying long horizons across episodes can limit opportunities for precise corrections. To address this limitation, we propose PICES (Perturbation-Informed Chunk and Execution Horizon Selection), a training-free method that jointly selects an action chunk and the number of actions executed before the next policy call. Within a single policy call, the action expert generates a batch of action chunks from multiple initial noise samples and their locally perturbed counterparts, using the same conditioning features across all samples. PICES exploits differences between corresponding actions in each nominal chunk and its counterpart to determine candidate-specific execution horizons and select a nominal chunk for execution. Experiments on simulation benchmarks and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate that PICES achieves speedup by up to 2.3x in wall-clock policy inference time on Jetson Orin and Thor relative to fixed horizon baselines while improving the success rate.

analysis.key_results: 在仿真基准和真实世界操作任务中，相比固定水平基线，PICES在Jetson Orin和Thor上实现最高2.3倍的策略推理时间加速，同时提高了成功率。

papers.abstract: Pre-trained robot policies, such as Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, provide a strong foundation for generalist robotic manipulation, but adapting them to new tasks with only a few demonstrations remains challenging. Directly fine-tuning a pre-trained policy often achieves strong in-distribution performance, yet it can distort the representations learned during pre-training and weaken the model's generalization ability under out-of-distribution shifts. We propose Retrieval-Anchored Representation Alignment (RARA), a two-stage adaptation method, to address this issue. First, RARA retrieves representation features from pretraining with similar task intent and motion, and aligns the policy's representations of the target demonstrations with the pre-trained representations of the retrieved demonstrations. Second, RARA fine-tunes the policy on the target demonstrations while limiting how much its representations of the retrieved demonstrations change during fine-tuning. By reducing the representation mismatch before action learning and preserving pre-trained knowledge during adaptation, RARA limits unnecessary representation drift during fine-tuning. Experiments with Diffusion Policy and GR00T on 13 tasks in RoboTwin, RoboCasa, and on a real robot show that RARA improves the average success of fine-tuning by 9.5 points in-distribution and 13.6 points out-of-distribution, and outperforms all compared baselines. Project page: https://shua-kang.github.io/RARA_robot/

analysis.key_results: 在RoboTwin、RoboCasa和真实机器人共13个任务上，Diffusion Policy和GR00T的微调平均成功率在分布内提升了9.5个百分点，在分布外提升了13.6个百分点，并优于所有对比基线。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出Retrieval-Anchored Representation Alignment (RARA)，一种两阶段适应方法，在微调前对齐目标演示与检索到的预训练演示表示，并在微调时限制检索表示的偏离，以减少表示漂移并提高泛化。
analysis.method: 首先从预训练数据中检索具有相似任务意图和运动的表示特征，并将目标演示的策略表示与检索到的预训练表示对齐；然后在微调时约束检索演示的表示变化，以保留预训练知识。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 提出了一种两阶段适应方法RARA，通过检索锚定表示对齐来减少预训练策略在少量演示微调时的表示漂移，从而提升机器人操作策略的分布内外泛化能力。
analysis.relation_to_vla_wam: 该方法直接针对VLA等预训练机器人策略的微调适应问题，通过表示对齐保留预训练知识并减少灾难性遗忘，对VLA模型的现实部署和高效适应具有直接相关性和实用价值。

papers.abstract: Generalizable robot manipulation requires predicting how a scene will evolve, identifying where interactions are feasible, and determining how to act. Action-labeled robot videos directly supervise control but are costly and limited in diversity, whereas egocentric human videos capture diverse interactions but lack robot actions and differ in embodiment and appearance. We introduce AffordanceWAM, an affordance-aware generative World Action Model that represents object-centric spatiotemporal affordance through Scalar Affordance and Affordance Heatmap, within the generated future World. This representation grounds visual prediction in task-relevantant objects and interaction regions for action generation, and provides shared interaction targets across human and robot videos. Built on a pretrained video diffusion Transformer, AffordanceWAM uses separately parameterized World and Action Experts, coupled through Masked Joint Self-Attention, to jointly predict future RGB observations, Scalar Affordance fields, Affordance Heatmaps, and continuous robot actions under a unified flow-matching objective. Human videos supervise all three future-World streams, whereas robot trajectories additionally provide action supervision, enabling transfer without human action labels or retargeting. Experiments on RoboCasa, CALVIN ABC$\rightarrow$D, and real-world manipulation demonstrate consistent gains over RGB-only and robot-data-only baselines. Under fixed robot supervision, RoboCasa performance improves monotonically as affordance-annotated human video scales. These results support affordance as an effective interface for both vision-language-action learning and human-to-robot transfer.

analysis.key_results: 在 RoboCasa、CALVIN ABC→D 和真实世界操作上相比仅 RGB 和仅机器人数据的基准取得一致提升；在固定机器人监督下，RoboCasa 性能随带可供性标注的人类视频规模单调提升。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出 AffordanceWAM，一种可供性感知的生成式世界动作模型，在统一的流匹配目标下联合预测未来 RGB 观测、标量可供性、可供性热图和连续动作，并实现从人类视频到机器人的跨域迁移。
analysis.method: 在预训练视频扩散 Transformer 上，使用分立参数化的世界专家和动作专家，通过掩码联合自注意力耦合，联合预测未来 RGB、标量可供性字段、可供性热图和连续机器人动作。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 提出可供性感知的生成式世界动作模型，通过标量可供性字段和可供性热图在预测的未来世界中联合生成机器人动作。
analysis.relation_to_vla_wam: 该论文以世界动作模型（WAM）为核心，通过可供性表示将世界建模与动作生成联合，并利用人类视频进行跨域迁移，与本站 VLA/WAM 和机器人世界建模主题高度相关。

papers.abstract: Agent memory systems have demonstrated significant potential in long-term dialogue, personalized assistants, and video understanding. However, continuously accumulated memory introduces substantial storage and retrieval costs during inference. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{MemForest}, a general memory compression framework adaptable to various agent memory systems. Specifically, MemForest partitions historical memory into event-centric units by leveraging global semantic similarity and local temporal continuity. For each unit, it constructs a maximum spanning tree, termed an EventTree, and progressively merges redundant memory nodes by selecting high-weight edges, reducing storage overhead. Furthermore, we introduce an anchor-guided propagation retrieval mechanism that retrieves relevant memory nodes from the temporal neighborhoods of key nodes, improving retrieval accuracy. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of MemForest. Under the unimodal Mem0 framework, MemForest retains \textbf{97.1%} of the original performance while compressing \textbf{50%} of historical memory across three benchmarks (LoCoMo, LongMemEval, and PersonaMem), achieving a \textbf{1.89x} retrieval speedup. Under the multimodal M3-Agent framework, it preserves \textbf{99.7%} of the original performance with a \textbf{50%} compression ratio across two benchmarks (M3-Bench-robot and M3-Bench-web), achieving a \textbf{2.24x} retrieval speedup. \textcolor{RoyalBlue}{\textit{Our code is available at [https://github.com/Celina-love-sweet/MemForest.}}](https://github.com/Celina-love-sweet/MemForest.}})

analysis.key_results: 在 Mem0（三个基准）上压缩 50% 记忆后保持 97.1% 原始性能，检索加速 1.89 倍；在 M3-Agent（含机器人基准）上压缩 50% 后保持 99.7% 性能，检索加速 2.24 倍。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出 MemForest 框架，将历史记忆按事件划分并构建最大生成树（EventTree），通过合并高权重边实现渐进压缩，并引入锚点引导传播检索机制以提高检索精度。
analysis.method: 事件树分区（基于全局语义相似度和局部时间连续性）、渐进合并记忆节点、锚点引导传播检索。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: MemForest 是一种通用智能体记忆压缩框架，通过事件树分区和渐进合并减少存储并加速检索。
analysis.relation_to_vla_wam: 该工作专注于智能体记忆压缩与检索加速，属于高效推理技术，但未直接涉及视觉-语言-动作（VLA）或世界-动作模型（WAM）。其多模态基准 M3-Bench-robot 涉及机器人任务，且摘要类别包含视觉-语言-机器人（composite），但与本站主题的 VLA/WAM 核心方向无直接研究关联。

papers.abstract: A central goal in robot learning is to move beyond task-specific human data collection toward robots that improve through autonomous interaction. Yet fully autonomous learning remains difficult with current policies: sparse rewards and weak zero-shot exploration often prevent online learning from discovering successful behavior. As a first step towards fully autonomous learning, we propose the minimal-data adaptation regime, in which a pretrained robot policy must learn a new task from as little as one demonstration followed by autonomous online interaction. We establish that, although pretrained policies fail zero-shot on many new tasks, a single demonstration suffices to direct their behavioral prior to coarse task-following behavior, albeit with unreliable performance. From this insight, we isolate the key design principles required to convert coarse task-following into reliable task success. These include (1) the surprising efficacy of pretrained VLA representations to support sample-efficient value learning from online interaction (2) the sufficiency of residual policy learning to learn corrective behavior and (3) the need for careful data-balancing to prevent exploration collapse. As a representative of these principles, we propose MiDAS, a simple offline-to-online RL recipe that combines few-demonstration behavior cloning with value-based residual learning over frozen VLA representations. Across LIBERO and RoboCasa tasks, MiDAS substantially improves performance from single-demonstration initializations, including policies that succeed only rarely, validating the principles highlighted above. On a bimanual YAM platform, starting from a brittle initial policy, MiDAS improves task success after approximately six hours of online interaction.

analysis.key_results: 在LIBERO和RoboCasa任务中，MiDAS从单次演示初始化大幅提升性能，包括原本很少成功的策略；在双臂YAM平台上，从脆弱的初始策略开始，约六小时在线交互后提高任务成功率。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出了最小数据适应设置，并确立了将粗略任务跟随转化为可靠任务成功的关键设计原则：利用预训练VLA表征进行样本高效值学习、残差策略学习以及防止探索崩溃的数据平衡。
analysis.method: MiDAS: 离线到在线强化学习配方，结合少量演示行为克隆与基于冻结VLA表征的值基残差学习。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 论文探讨了预训练VLA策略在单次演示和在线交互的最小数据环境下适应新任务所需的原理，并提出MiDAS方法。
analysis.relation_to_vla_wam: 论文直接围绕预训练VLA策略的高效适应展开，使用冻结的VLA表征进行值学习和残差策略学习，对VLA在真实机器人上的快速部署和持续学习具有直接方法学价值。

papers.abstract: Organizations that cannot send data to a cloud API need to know how well self-hosted open-weight models perform on Text-to-SQL and which inexpensive techniques justify their compute. We benchmark Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct (7B, 14B, 32B) and CodeLlama-Instruct (7B, 13B) self-hosted at 16-bit precision, Llama-3.1-8B and Llama-3.3-70B through an FP8 API, and Qwen2.5-Coder-32B through a second API on the BIRD development split (n = 1534), with one zero-shot prompt and the official execution-accuracy comparison on read-only databases. We ablate lexical and embedding schema linking, execution-guided self-correction and self-consistency, and test every within-model recipe difference with exact McNemar tests, Holm correction over 30 tests and a database-clustered bootstrap. Qwen2.5-Coder reaches 42.6%, 52.0% and 54.9%; CodeLlama-7B and -13B reach 23.7% and 26.3%. Self-correction is the only component with a consistent gain: within a run it adds 1.2 to 4.4 points at 1.1 to 1.9 times the tokens, and it is significant after Holm correction for every model except Llama-3.3-70B. Schema linking never helps significantly; lexical linking costs Llama-3.3-70B 4.2 points, and an embedding linker with higher table recall does not differ detectably from no linking. Self-consistency, run for one model, changed accuracy by at most 0.13 points at about five times the tokens. One API provider dropped spaces next to digits; after a whitespace repair the same model scored 54.5% through the API and 54.9% self-hosted, so an apparent three-point serving gap was mostly this defect. This version corrects six defects of v1, including writable databases, a stricter-than-official metric and a truncated API arm, and withdraws the v1 claim of a quantization penalty of about 13 points; all numbers are re-scored or re-run. Code, per-item predictions and analysis scripts are released.

analysis.key_results: Qwen2.5-Coder达到42.6%、52.0%和54.9%；CodeLlama-7B和-13B分别达到23.7%和26.3%。自纠正是唯一持续有效的技巧，添加1.2到4.4个点，代价为1.1到1.9倍的token。模式链接从未显著帮助；自一致性对精度影响最多0.13个点。修复API提供方的空格缺陷后，同一模型得分54.5%（API）和54.9%（自托管）。
analysis.main_contribution: 在BIRD开发集上对Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct和CodeLlama-Instruct等自托管开源模型进行了系统基准测试，并消融了多种推理技巧，修正了v1版本中的缺陷。
analysis.method: 在16位精度下自托管开源模型，并使用FP8 API对比，采用零样本提示和执行准确率评估，通过McNemar检验和Holm校正进行统计显著性测试。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 该论文在BIRD基准上评估了自托管开源LLM的Text-to-SQL性能，并消融了模式链接、自纠正和自一致性等技巧。
analysis.relation_to_vla_wam: 该论文专注于Text-to-SQL任务的开源LLM评估和技巧消融，与VLA（视觉-语言-动作）和WAM（机器人世界模型）无直接关系。但其涉及的模型量化（FP8 API）和高效推理技巧（自纠正、自一致性）对本站关于模型量化和高效推理的主题具有一定的参考价值。

papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models leverage the rich world knowledge of pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) to enable instruction-following robotic manipulation. However, the structural mismatch between VLM semantic spaces and embodied control policies often hinders the learning of precise perception-action mappings. To address this challenge, we propose AffordanceVLA, a scalable, unified framework that introduces structured affordance learning as a task-oriented and object-centric intermediate representation to establish a more precise and robust perception-action mapping. Specifically, we progressively model manipulation priors through three complementary components - Which2Act, Where2Act, and How2Act - which jointly produce spatially grounded, semantically conditioned, and action-coupled intermediate representations, thereby naturally bridging vision, language, and action. We integrate these modules into a Mixture-of-Transformer (MoT) architecture and adopt a three-stage progressive training curriculum that leverages 8.8M affordance-centric grounding and pointing samples, translating scalable vision-language supervision into improved robotic manipulation. To overcome the scarcity of dense affordance labels in robotic datasets, we also develop a robust automated data augmentation pipeline. Extensive experiments on ID & OOD simulation and real-world demonstrate that AffordanceVLA outperforms strong VLA baselines across diverse manipulation scenarios, validating structured affordance learning as a scalable and robust bridge that integrates multi-source vision-language supervision while connecting pretrained VLM semantics to embodied robot control.

analysis.key_results: 在 ID 和 OOD 仿真及真实世界的大量实验中，AffordanceVLA 在多种操作场景下优于强 VLA 基线。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出 AffordanceVLA 框架，通过 Which2Act、Where2Act、How2Act 三个互补模块引入结构化可供性学习，并采用 Mixture-of-Transformer 架构和三阶段渐进训练课程，将大规模视觉-语言监督转化为改进的机器人操作能力。
analysis.method: 通过三个互补组件（Which2Act、Where2Act、How2Act）建模操作先验，生成空间接地、语义条件和动作耦合的中间表示；采用 Mixture-of-Transformer 架构和三阶段渐进训练；利用 8.8M 可供性为中心的接地和指向样本进行训练；开发自动化数据增强流程以克服机器人数据集中密集可供性标签稀缺的问题。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: AffordanceVLA 提出结构化可供性学习框架，以任务导向、对象中心的中间表示桥接视觉、语言与动作，从而提升机器人操作策略的精确性和鲁棒性。
analysis.relation_to_vla_wam: 本文直接针对 VLA 模型，旨在解决 VLM 语义空间与具体控制策略之间的结构失配问题，通过结构化可供性学习建立更精确的感知-动作映射，与本站主题高度相关。
